arxiv-2101-05168.title: The interior-boundary Strichartz estimate for the Schrödinger equation on the half line revisited Thanks: TÖ’s research is partially supported by the Science Academy’s Young Scientist Award Program (BAGEP 2020)
arxiv-2101-05168.creator: Bİlge Köksal and Türker Özsarı
arxiv-2101-05168.description: Abstract . It was shown by the second author in [ 24 ] for the biharmonic Schrödinger equation and most recently by Himonas and Mantzavinos [ 14 ] for 2D Schrödinger equation that Fokas method based formulas are capable of defining weak solutions of associated nonlinear initial boundary value problems (ibvps) below the Banach algebra threshold.

arxiv-2111-10110.title: Reformulated Fourier Modal Method with improved near field computations
arxiv-2111-10110.creator: Sergey Spiridonov, Alexey A. Shcherbakov
arxiv-2111-10110.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Sergey Spiridonov, Alexey A. Shcherbakov. In this paper we propose a new formulation of the Fourier Modal Method based on an alternative treatment of interface conditions allowing us to overcome the effect of the Gibbs phenomenon. Explicit consideration of the interface conditions for the discontinuous part of the field leads to an equation for the eigenvalue problem, which can be written in an inversion-free form.

arxiv-2211-09322.title: Targeted Attention for Generalized- and Zero-Shot Learning
arxiv-2211-09322.creator: Abhijit Suprem
arxiv-2211-09322.description: Abstract The Zero-Shot Learning (ZSL) task attempts to learn concepts without any labeled data. Unlike traditional classification/detection tasks, the evaluation environment is provided unseen classes never encountered during training (in the related Generalized ZSL, or GZSL, setting, both seen and unseen classes are provided).

arxiv-2307-12043.title: Euler and the Duplication Formula for the Gamma-Function
arxiv-2307-12043.creator: Alexander Aycock, Johannes-Gutenberg University Mainz
arxiv-2307-12043.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Alexander Aycock, Johannes-Gutenberg University Mainz. We show how the formulas in Euler’s paper "Variae considerationes circa series hypergeometricas" [ 4 ] imply Legendre’s duplication formula for the Γ \Gamma -function. This paper can be seen as an Addendum to [ 2 ] . 1 Introduction In [ 2 ] , we focused on a function defined by Euler in [ 4 ] as: \Gamma_{E}(x):=a\cdot(a+b)\cdot(a+2b)\cdot(a+3b)\cdot\cdots\cdot(a+(x-1)b)\quad\text{for}\quad a,b>0, (1) which we showed to be continueable to non-integer values of x via the expression: \Gamma_{E}(x)=\dfrac{b^{x}}{\Gamma\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)}\cdot\Gamma\left(x+\dfrac{a}{b}\right).

arxiv-2311-06890.title: Distributed Sequential Receding Horizon Control of Multi-Agent Systems under Recurring Signal Temporal Logic
arxiv-2311-06890.creator: Eleftherios E. Vlahakis, Lars Lindemann, Dimos V. Dimarogonas
arxiv-2311-06890.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Eleftherios E. Vlahakis, Lars Lindemann, Dimos V. Dimarogonas. We consider the synthesis problem of a multi-agent system under signal temporal logic (STL) specifications representing bounded-time tasks that need to be satisfied recurrently over an infinite horizon. Motivated by the limited approaches to handling recurring STL systematically, we tackle the infinite-horizon control problem with a receding horizon scheme equipped with additional STL constraints that introduce minimal complexity and a backward-reachability-based terminal condition that is straightforward to construct and ensures recursive feasibility.

arxiv-2401-09293.title: Restricted Mean Value Property with non-tangential boundary behavior on Riemannian manifolds
arxiv-2401-09293.creator: Utsav Dewan
arxiv-2401-09293.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Utsav Dewan. A well studied classical problem is the harmonicity of functions satisfying the restricted mean-value property (RMVP) for domains in ℝ n \mathbb{R}^{n} . Recently, the author along with Biswas investigated the problem in the general setting of Riemannian manifolds and obtained results in terms of unrestricted boundary limits of the function on a full measure subset of the boundary.

arxiv-2409-17449.title: Stringy Hodge numbers of Pfaffian double mirrors and Homological Projective Duality
arxiv-2409-17449.creator: Zengrui Han
arxiv-2409-17449.description: Abstract . We study the stringy Hodge numbers of Pfaffian double mirrors, generalizing previous results of Borisov and Libgober. In the even-dimensional cases, we introduce a modified version of stringy E E -functions and obtain interesting relations between the modified stringy E E -functions on the two sides.

arxiv-2411-09939.title: Self-similar groupoid actions on k k -graphs, and invariance of K K -theory for cocycle homotopies Thanks: This research was supported by Australian Research Council grant DP220101631. The first author was supported by University of Wollongong AEGiS CONNECT grant 141765
arxiv-2411-09939.creator: Alexander Mundey, Aidan Sims
arxiv-2411-09939.description: Abstract . We establish conditions under which an inclusion of finitely aligned left-cancellative small categories induces inclusions of twisted C ∗ C^{*} -algebras. We also present an example of an inclusion of finitely aligned left-cancellative monoids that does not induce a homomorphism even between (untwisted) Toeplitz algebras.

arxiv-2510-00411.title: Does Bigger Mean Better? Comparitive Analysis of CNNs and Biomedical Vision Language Modles in Medical Diagnosis
arxiv-2510-00411.creator: Ran Tong, Jiaqi Liu, Su Liu, Jiexi Xu, Lanruo Wang, Tong Wang
arxiv-2510-00411.description: Abstract The accurate interpretation of chest radiographs using automated methods is a critical task in medical imaging. This paper presents a comparative analysis between a supervised lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and a state-of-the-art, zero-shot medical Vision-Language Model (VLM), BiomedCLIP, across two distinct diagnostic tasks: pneumonia detection on the PneumoniaMNIST benchmark and tuberculosis detection on the Shenzhen TB dataset.

arxiv-2511-11139.title: Speech-Aware Long Context Pruning and Integration for Contextualized Automatic Speech Recognition
arxiv-2511-11139.creator: Yiming Rong, Yixin Zhang, Ziyi Wang, Deyang Jiang, Yunlong Zhao, Haoran Wu, Shiyu Zhou, Bo Xu
arxiv-2511-11139.description: Abstract Automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems have achieved remarkable performance in common conditions but often struggle to leverage long-context information in contextualized scenarios that require domain-specific knowledge, such as conference presentations. This challenge arises primarily due to constrained model context windows and the sparsity of relevant information within extensive contextual noise.

arxiv-2601-21172.title: Magnonic Quantum Spin Hall Effect with Chiral Magnon Transport in Bilayer Altermagnets
arxiv-2601-21172.creator: Bo Yuan, Yingxi Bai, Ying Dai, Baibiao Huang, Chengwang Niu
arxiv-2601-21172.description: Abstract Altermagnetism has attracted considerable interest, yet its associated spintronic phenomena have so far been largely confined to electronic systems. In this work, we uncover a universal symmetry-based strategy for realizing topological altermagnets with the magnonic quantum spin Hall effect, as evidenced by a nonzero spin Chern number and protected helical edge states.

Here, we developed new technology to determine PTK activity profiles using peptid

pmc-10663827.title: Exploring the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on energy literacy and conservation behavior in academic buildings of Kuwait
pmc-10663827.creator: Majdi M Alomari, Hania EL-Kanj, Ayse Topal, Nafesah I Alshdaifat
pmc-10663827.description: This study investigates the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on energy literacy and conservation behavior among occupant groups in academic buildings in Kuwait. It explores influential factors, focusing on the pandemic's effect on attitudes, intentions, and behaviors related to energy conservation. The research adopts a mixed-methods approach, incorporating quantitative and qualitative data collection methods.

pmc-11393426.title: PEG-SeNPs as therapeutic agents inhibiting apoptosis and inflammation of cells infected with H1N1 influenza A virus
pmc-11393426.creator: Min Guo, Yu-Dan Ye, Jian-Piao Cai, Hai-Tong Xu, Wei Wei, Jia-Yu Sun, Chen-Yang Wang, Chang-Bing Wang, Ying-Hua Li, Bing Zhu
pmc-11393426.description: The rapid variation of influenza challenges vaccines and treatments, which makes an urgent task to develop the high-efficiency and low-toxicity new anti-influenza virus drugs. Selenium is one of the essential trace elements for the human body that possesses a good antiviral activity.

pmc-11455072.title: 7487 Iatrogenic Cushing’s Syndrome In A Patient On Prezcobix And Fluticasone
pmc-11455072.creator: A N Davis, M Nicholson
pmc-11455072.description: Disclosure: A.N. Davis: None. M. Nicholson: None. Introduction: The HIV medication Prezcobix contains darunavir, a protease inhibitor which is known to inhibit the hepatic enzyme CYP3A4. This may lead to accumulation of some medications in the blood, including fluticasone. We present a patient with iatrogenic Cushing’s syndrome while on Prezcobix and fluticasone.

pmc-11478640.title: Compression Behavior of 3D Printed Composite Isogrid Structures
pmc-11478640.creator: Marina Andreozzi, Carlo Bruni, Archimede Forcellese, Serena Gentili, Alessio Vita
pmc-11478640.description: Composite materials, particularly carbon fiber-reinforced polymers (CFRPs), have become a cornerstone in industries requiring high-performance materials due to their exceptional mechanical properties, such as high strength-to-weight ratios, and their inherent lightweight nature. These attributes make CFRPs highly desirable in aerospace, automotive, and other advanced engineering applications.

pmc-11480445.title: Nitrogen signaling factor triggers a respiration-like gene expression program in fission yeast
pmc-11480445.creator: Shin Ohsawa, Michaela Schwaiger, Vytautas Iesmantavicius, Rio Hashimoto, Hiromitsu Moriyama, Hiroaki Matoba, Go Hirai, Mikiko Sodeoka, Atsushi Hashimoto, Akihisa Matsuyama, Minoru Yoshida, Yoko Yashiroda, Marc Bühler
pmc-11480445.description: Microbes have evolved intricate communication systems that enable individual cells of a population to send and receive signals in response to changes in their immediate environment. In the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe, the oxylipin nitrogen signaling factor (NSF) is part of such communication system, which functions to regulate the usage of different nitrogen sources.

pmc-11512777.title: Association Between Gallstones and Depressive Symptoms: Results from NHANES and Mendelian Randomization Study
pmc-11512777.creator: Ruidong Ma, Wei Li, Qiufeng Peng, Ao Ren, Ling Zhao, Jiawei Li, Shiqiao Luo
pmc-11512777.description: PurposePrior research has suggested a correlation between gallstones and depressive symptoms, yet the specifics of this relationship remain unclear. This study aims to explore the association between gallstones and depressive symptoms among adults.Patients and MethodsInitially, we conducted a cross-sectional study using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2017 – March 2020.

pmc-13071209.title: Crosstalk Between Auditory and Visual information in Motor Learning and Savings
pmc-13071209.creator: Olivier White
pmc-13071209.description: Sensorimotor adaptation relies on the integration of multisensory feedback, yet the specific contributions of auditory signals to this process remain poorly understood compared to vision. We tested 46 participants on a reaching task using visual, auditory, or combined feedback about terminal errors. Participants alternated between feedback modalities during learning and relearning, revealing how adaptation transfers across sensory systems.

pmc-13254259.title: The current status of foundation models in decoding inner speech from non-invasive brain signals: a mini review
pmc-13254259.creator: Esra Sümer-Arpak, Rajkumar Saini, Debashis Das Chakladar, Sanjeev Kumar Varun, Foteini Simistira Liwicki
pmc-13254259.description: Inner speech (IS), or imagined speech without overt articulation, is a promising target for brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) aimed at restoring communication in individuals with severe speech impairments, such as locked-in syndrome. Foundation models (FMs), typically trained using self-supervised learning (SSL) on large-scale datasets, offer new opportunities for learning transferable and robust representations from neural signals.

pmc-13356319.title: Rhupus syndrome presenting with anterior scleritis and lupus nephritis: A case report
pmc-13356319.creator: Myrah Sheriff, Veena Patel
pmc-13356319.description: Rhupus syndrome is a rare disease that presents with features of both rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus. It is typically characterized by a rheumatoid arthritis pattern of symmetric, polyarticular small joint pain and swelling along with features of lupus such as photosensitive skin rashes and hematologic abnormalities.

pmc-13603471.title: Melatonin Attenuates Cadmium-Induced Oxidative Stress in Potato by Remodeling Redox Homeostasis and Activating Multi-Pathway Antioxidant Networks
pmc-13603471.creator: Panfeng Yao, Junmei Cui, Wenlin Li, Jianguo Wei, Ying Wang, Chao Sun, Zhenzhen Bi, Zhen Liu, Han Wang, Yuhui Liu, Jiangping Bai
pmc-13603471.description: Cadmium pollution severely suppresses potato growth, impairs photosynthesis, and disrupts cellular redox balance, threatening crop yield and food safety. Exogenous small-molecule regulators represent low-cost strategies to alleviate heavy-metal phytotoxicity, yet systematic comparisons of N-acetyl-L-cysteine (NAC), L-tryptophan (Trp), and melatonin (MT) on Cd-stressed potatoes remain insufficient.
